ChurchStream is free software for **Seventh-day Adventist churches**: live streaming to YouTube and Facebook plus projection of hymns, Bible readings and announcements, from one simple control panel. It runs on Windows and Mac.

## Download

| Computer | Download |
|---|---|
| **Windows** laptop or PC | **[ChurchStream-win-x64.zip](https://github.com/driviere/churchStream/releases/download/v0.3.6/ChurchStream-win-x64.zip)** |
| **Mac with an Apple chip** (M1–M4) | **[ChurchStream-mac-arm64.zip](https://github.com/driviere/churchStream/releases/download/v0.3.6/ChurchStream-mac-arm64.zip)** |
| **Mac with an Intel processor** | **[ChurchStream-mac-x64.zip](https://github.com/driviere/churchStream/releases/download/v0.3.6/ChurchStream-mac-x64.zip)** |

**Updating?** Copy the new files over your old ChurchStream folder; your **ChurchStream-data** folder (settings, songs, services) is kept. First time? See the install steps in the [README](https://github.com/driviere/churchStream#install-windows).

## New in 0.3.6: a real Mac app

On a Mac, ChurchStream is now **ChurchStream.app**, a normal Mac app. It starts without a Terminal window, so Terminal settings (such as oh-my-zsh's update question) can no longer stop it from starting.

**Installing or updating on a Mac**
1. Download the zip for your Mac (Apple chip or Intel) and unzip it.
2. Drag **ChurchStream.app** into your **Applications** folder.
3. Double-click it. The first time, macOS may say it can't verify the app: open **System Settings → Privacy & Security**, scroll down and click **Open Anyway** (or Control-click the app, choose **Open**, then **Open** again).
4. Click **OK** when it asks about the camera and microphone, and **Allow** for incoming network connections and the local network.

**Using it**
- ChurchStream shows in the **Dock** while it runs. Closed the browser tab? Click the Dock icon to open the control panel again.
- To stop everything, choose **ChurchStream → Quit** (or Control-click the Dock icon → Quit).
- Your settings, songs, services and recordings are now kept in **ChurchStream-data** in your home folder (Finder → Go → Home), so installing a newer app keeps them. Data from your old ChurchStream folder is copied there the first time you open the app.
- *Start ChurchStream.command* is still included as another way to start it in Terminal.

Windows is unchanged.

## Good to know
- Projecting or streaming hymns still under copyright needs your church's **CCLI** licence (and the Streaming Licence for online use).
- ChurchStream is an independent project, not an official product of the Seventh-day Adventist Church.
